findings.body: The doc comment lists `off`, `low`, `medium`, `high` as the only valid values, but the field is a plain `String`.  A malformed value (e.g. `"hight"`, `"default"`) would pass schema or structure validation and reach the inference path where it either triggers a provider error or, worse, is silently ignored and falls into undefined behaviour.  The repository’s own convention in `vendor/tinyhivemind` already treats these as an enum.  Making `reasoning_effort` a `ReasoningEffort` enum or newtype that serde-deserializes from the four strings would eliminate a class of bugs without changing the serialization format.  The fix applies only to the added field, so the `existing_code` span is just that line.
findings.title: Enforce the allowed values for reasoning_effort with an enum or newtype

value.summary: The change adds a `reasoning_effort` field to `ModelConfig` as a `String`, but the field is validated nowhere against the enum it describes, and the diff provides no documentation of how this string maps to actual model behaviour.  A typo like `"hight"` would silently produce undefined behaviour at inference time.  Until the field carries a newtype or an enum that enforces `off | low | medium | high`, the author should know about this untracked failure path.
